A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FCENet study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The separate supplementary material mentioned in v1 is not included, so its removal or revision cannot be inferred.

before.justification: v1 reports original frequency-correlation analyses, DVD and IVRG denoising results, real-world qualitative comparisons, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original analyses and experiments, including quantitative benchmark results and ablations, and reports per-image PSNR values in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Equation 6 changes the reported objective: the frequency-domain loss acts on the pre-denoising output in v1 but on the final network output in v2. The architecture and fusion procedures otherwise remain unchanged; CRM/DRM are renamed CFR/DFR. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a formula correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate simulated denoising on DVD and IVRG and qualitative denoising on real low-light RGB/NIR pairs. Replacing examples in Figure 6 does not introduce a different dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same four single-image baselines and five NIR-assisted baselines. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the qualitative comparisons and ablations; updated citations and mechanism names do not introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, noise models and levels, 128×128 training patches, batch size 16, 80/100 training epochs, learning-rate schedules, and PSNR/SSIM evaluation remain unchanged. The stated 64/36-channel model configurations are retained; the revised parameter-count result does not establish a changed evaluation configuration.

E4.justification: Figure 6 replaces the first two DVD examples, revising the qualitative case evidence concerning detail recovery, color restoration, and artifact suppression. Tables 3–5 and the filter/feature analyses in Figures 8–9 are unchanged. The new misalignment discussion is not accompanied by a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Both retain the same description of randomly selecting 30 image pairs for the frequency-correlation analysis.

E6.justification: All PSNR/SSIM entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. Table 1 revises FCENet's parameter count from 4.32M to 4.44M. Figure 6 updates displayed cases and adds per-image PSNR values, including FCENet scores of 34.05, 28.18, and 29.93 dB; these are newly reported example results, not demonstrated improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 6 substantively revises the formal loss definition by assigning its frequency-domain penalty to a different network output. Equations 1–5 and their mathematical reasoning otherwise remain equivalent after notation changes. No new assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The frequency-correlation prior, FDSM and FEFM contributions, and claims of superior denoising with computational efficiency are retained. The experimental contribution formerly presented as a fourth bullet moves into nearby prose rather than being withdrawn.

C2.justification: The v2 conclusion adds a specific applicability concern: existing methods may fail on significantly misaligned cross-field images. It proposes feature-point matching or deformable convolution as future remedies. The interpretations of the retained benchmark and ablation results otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The generic promise to release code becomes a specific FCENet GitHub release location, still described as a future release. Conversely, v2 removes the NVIDIA RTX 3090 hardware disclosure and the explicit list of IVRG scene categories. Most implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Noise2Self, Zero-shot Noise2Noise, Positive2Negative, and classical denoising work, while removing Rahimi–Recht's random-features paper and Yan et al.'s hyperspectral frequency-correlation paper. The central positioning against indiscriminate fusion and common-feature-only fusion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and grammar revisions throughout, renames CRM/DRM to CFR/DFR, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes the contribution paragraph. The section hierarchy and overall explanatory sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 swaps and relabels its plots, Figure 5 explicitly depicts the transpose already present in Equation 4, and Figure 6 changes examples and adds PSNR rows. Tables adopt citation labels. Figure 3 introduces a caption error: its descriptions of panels (a) and (b) are reversed relative to the plotted titles.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves interpretability through the clearer fusion schematic and per-image PSNR annotations, and adds a useful applicability boundary concerning severe RGB/NIR misalignment. Benchmark accuracy and ablation evidence remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited. Removal of the GPU disclosure and the new Figure 3 caption reversal reduce these benefits; the plot titles and surrounding frequency-trend explanation remain correct.
